data.content_ref: inline:SRC_001 proposes a difficulty × accuracy-differential interaction test as the single-evaluation discriminator, but this fails the school's demand for a causal mechanism. The transfer claim asserts 'genuine reliability gain is difficulty-amplifying; mere compliance is difficulty-attenuating' without any causal derivation. The analogy's own overturn conditions concede the interaction need not be monotonic, which undercuts the discriminative power. More fundamentally, if checklist features are causal but co-occur with incidental features that also correlate with outcomes, the interaction is confounded: an interaction effect could be driven by the incidental co-variation rather than by whether the checklist mechanism is genuinely tracking the outcome. No causal mechanism — e.g., an intervention on checklist coverage that would shift the outcome distribution — is specified that would rule out this confound.
